PostToolUse._comment: Hook 1: Warn when console.log is found in TypeScript or JavaScript files after any edit or write. Prints a warning with matching line numbers. Catches debug statements before they accumulate.

hooks.command: file="${CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT_file_path:-${CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT_path:-}}"; if [[ "$file" =~ \.(ts|tsx|js|jsx)$ ]]; then matches=$(grep -n 'console\.log' "$file" 2>/dev/null | head -3); if [ -n "$matches" ]; then echo "[WARN] console.log found in $file:"; echo "$matches"; fi; fi

PostToolUse._comment: Hook 2: Remind to update INDEX.md when a new file is written. Only fires when SESSION.md exists (meaning this is a memory-enabled project) and the written file is not SESSION.md or INDEX.md itself.

hooks.command: file="${CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT_file_path:-}"; sess=$(find . -name 'SESSION.md' -path '*/obsidian/*' 2>/dev/null | head -1); if [ -n "$sess" ] && [[ "$file" != *SESSION.md* ]] && [[ "$file" != *INDEX.md* ]]; then echo "[MEMORY] New file written: $file — update obsidian/INDEX.md if this is a new module, route, or service"; fi

Stop._comment: Hook 3: Update the _Last updated: timestamp in SESSION.md every time Claude Code finishes a response or the session ends. Ensures the timestamp is accurate even if the session is interrupted. Uses BSD sed syntax (macOS). On Linux, change 'sed -i ''' to 'sed -i'.

hooks.command: ts=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M'); sess=$(find . -name 'SESSION.md' -path '*/obsidian/*' 2>/dev/null | head -1); if [ -n "$sess" ]; then sed -i '' "s/^_Last updated:.*/_Last updated: $ts/" "$sess" 2>/dev/null; fi
